answer: Agents can require each new account to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. A mesa of cheap identities no longer creates free influence: each one needs capital at risk, and splitting the same stake across accounts does not increase voting weight. The signal is costly to fake because a raven-like attacker must acquire more tokens and expose each deposit to loss, making large-scale Sybil attacks expensive rather than merely computational.
